name: @projexlight/sdk-config
summary: Unified multi-scope configuration & secrets plane (EP-341). Stores config values and secret references at four scopes — platform, tenant, app and app_user — and resolves the most-specific active value along the app_user -> app -> tenant -> platform precedence chain. Backs provider bindings (payment, email, AI-gateway) so runtime handlers return a debuggable 503 PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED instead of a 500 when a provider is unset.

endpoints.description: Resolve the most-specific active value for a key in the caller's context, walking app_user -> app -> tenant -> platform.
List the active config rows for a given scope (platform|tenant|app|app_user), defaulting scope_id from the caller's JWT.
Fetch a single config row by exact scope/scope_id/key; 404 when no active row exists.
Upsert a config value (non-secret `value`) or secret pointer (`secret_ref`) at a scope; ownership-guarded per scope (platform operators / owning-tenant admins / the user themselves).
Soft-delete (revoke) a config value so it no longer resolves; ownership-guarded.
Rotate a secret value's envelope pointer (secret_ref) in place without changing the key; ownership-guarded.

models.description: One row per (scope, scope_id, key) with a jsonb value or a secret_ref, status and set_by audit; UNIQUE(scope, scope_id, key).

scenarios.title: Resolve a value along the scope precedence chain
scenarios.when_to_use: When a runtime handler needs the effective value of a key for the current caller, honouring app_user overrides before falling back to app, tenant, then platform defaults.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns the most-specific active row (or null). row.scope names the winning level and row.value carries the resolved jsonb, so the caller knows both the value and where it came from.

scenarios.title: Set a tenant provider and guard a handler with a debuggable 503
scenarios.when_to_use: When a feature (payments, email, AI-gateway) must not run until its provider is configured, and you want a clear 503 the operator can act on rather than an opaque 500.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Before setConfig the guard returns a { error: 'PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED', provider_key, message, scopes_checked } body (send it as 503). After setConfig the guard returns null and the handler proceeds.

scenarios.title: Store a secret reference and rotate it in place
scenarios.when_to_use: When a scope needs to point at a secret held in the sdk-secrets envelope store (an API key, webhook secret) and later rotate the pointer without changing the key or its consumers.
scenarios.expected_outcome: The config row keeps the same (scope, scope_id, key) but its secret_ref now points at the new envelope; resolveConfig returns the rotated secret_ref and never the plaintext secret.

compliance_posture.notes: Stores configuration and secret POINTERS (secret_ref) only — never plaintext secrets, which live in the sdk-secrets envelope store. Rows are tenant/app/user scoped and soft-deleted (revoked) rather than hard-deleted, preserving set_by/status audit. Config values may hold tenant business data, so treat exports under GDPR data-subject scope.
